_comment: How well the society works and how people feel about it. Add a quality or a satisfaction meter here and the engine, NPCs and HUD pick it up. All values run 0-100. 'supply_curve': a supply-style quality is 100 x (supply / need) ^ supply_curve (below 1, the first workers count most).

quality_events._comment: Something that happens hits a quality at once by its 'events' points (a death: Care -10). The chunk is not a constant drain: it comes back by itself, halving every 'recover_half_life_life_hours' hours of the day-night cycle (12 = about a year and a half).

work_quality._comment: How well one person does one job or office: their weighted attributes (share 'attribute_share') and skill (share 'skill_share'), scaled down when they are unwell ('condition': how much health and energy matter).

qualities._comment: Society-wide qualities. style 'supply': the work of 'sources' (occupations, or 'office:Name') against what the group needs ('per_person' x members); each worker gives 'amount' x their work quality / 50. 'variety': share of the score that depends on how many 'category' kinds are covered. style 'offices': the average quality of every office seat (vacant seats count as 0), weighted by the office's points. 'weight': importance in the overall society score. 'requires': innovations before it counts. A source's 'while_working': its workers count this many times over while they are doing their job's work right now (a Warrior out on patrol, the Spirit Keeper leading a ritual). Jobs and offices with work of their own (work.json) count only while worked lately. 'on_hand' (food): part of the value comes from what the tribe actually holds.

on_hand._comment: 'share' of the Food quality comes from the food the tribe actually holds (camp store and everyone's packs) against 'per_member' food points each (140 = two meals), the rest from the work being done. Without it Food can read full while people go hungry, and leaders see no need for more food workers.

'share' of the Water quality comes from the water the tribe holds (camp store and packs) against 'per_member' water points each (640 = four day-night cycles' drinking, about 21 water each), the rest from Gatherers fetching it (a Gatherer counts 'amount' 0.5: they forage and gather wood too). Leaders see a water shortage through this and put more people on it. Scaled back on 2026-11-16: it used to reach 100 within half a year.

fire.name: Fire
fire._comment: The tribe is content with its fire only by using it: each time someone warms up at the fire ('uses': care:warm_up) it rises 'per_use' points. Otherwise it stays the same ('fall_per_day' 0; set it above 0 to let it fade when nobody uses the fire). A fire merely burning adds nothing. It begins at 'start'. 'sources' only says whose work it rests on (the Firekeeper keeps the fire people use).

sick._comment: 'share' of the Care quality comes from how well the sick are seen to (data/life.json 'illnesses'): 100 less 'per_sick' for each person ill now who has nobody to see to them. Healing work worth 'cover_supply' (about one Healer at work) sees to them all. So Care can't read full while people lie sick with no Healer, and leaders see the need for one (and the cost of taking one away).

events._comment: Points taken out at once when this happens (one big chunk, not a constant drain; it comes back slowly, see 'quality_events'). 'death': anyone dying.

hardship._comment: Hard times drag contentment down fast, on top of a meter's normal movement (user's rule, 2026-11-16). Each meter may list 'hardship': while its 'source' is below 'below', the meter loses up to 'fall_per_day_at_zero' per day-night cycle (all of it at 0, in proportion above) and can't sit more than 'cap_above' above the source. Sources: 'need:<need>' (Comfort: warmth, freezing), 'health' (Food, Work, Comfort, Leaders: the weak and sick), 'tribe_distress' (Society, Leaders: 100 less the share of the tribe in distress, someone being ill, below a critical need, or under 'weak_below' health). Faster-falling Leaders and Society run out patience sooner, so NPCs turn on those in charge before the tribe dies out.

satisfaction._comment: Each person's contentment meters (0-100). Most meters move toward a target: the weighted average of their 'inputs', closing 'rise_per_day' of the gap per day-night cycle while below it (times every 'multipliers' factor) and 'fall_per_day' while above it (both default to 'drift_per_day'). Inputs: 'quality:<name>' or 'society' (the society qualities above), 'need:<name>' or 'needs' (their own body), 'meter:<key>' (another of their meters), 'own_work' (how well they do their best job; 'no_work' if none), 'working' and 'fire' (see 'input_values'), 'positions_filled' (see 'positions'). 'bonus' adds points: 'holds_office'. 'expectations': false leaves out what they have grown used to. A person's 'grievances' (see 'job_loss') lower a meter's target. Multipliers (each a 'curve' of [x, multiplier] points, read as a line between them): 'tools' (x = how many tools for their job they carry; 'none_invented' while no tool for it exists yet), 'job_variety' (x = share of the age's occupations open, see 'job_variety'), 'fit' (x = how well they do their job, 0-100; 'appointed_only': only for work a leader appointed them to), 'positions_filled' (x = share filled), 'meters_rising' (x = share of the meters it takes as inputs that are rising), 'working_now:<job>' (x = how many people are doing that job's work right now; offices as 'office:<name>').

input_values._comment: What the special inputs are worth (0-100). 'working': while the person is doing their own job's work right now (the W key: a task or recipe of their occupation or office), while they hold a job but are not working it, and while they have none. 'fire': while the fire burns and a Firekeeper has tended it lately (worked within work.json 'work_counts_life_hours'), while it burns untended, and while it is out.

positions._comment: 'positions_filled' (an input and a multiplier): the share of the tribe's positions that are filled. Positions are every seat of every unlocked office ('office_seats') and every unlocked occupation ('occupations'; filled while anyone holds it, and not counted while nobody could take it up for want of a tool). 'cap_at_members': a tribe can't fill more positions than it has members, so the share is out of at most that many.

job_variety._comment: 'job_variety' (a multiplier): how many occupations are open (researched) out of every occupation of the ages reached so far. An occupation belongs to the latest age among the innovations it requires (or occupations.json 'age'). So it is relative to the age: 10 open of the Tribal Age's 10 is everything, but the same 10 of a later age's 25 is little choice.

food.name: Food
food._comment: 'variety_rates': instead of drifting toward a target, this meter moves by this many points per day-night cycle, by how many kinds of food the person carries right now (0 kinds, 1, 2, 3, 4 or more): nothing to eat makes people unhappy fast, one kind barely holds them, a varied pack pleases them more and more. 'hunger': once their 'need' (food) is below 'below', the meter also falls by up to 'fall_per_day_at_zero' points per cycle (all of it when starving), and can't be more than 'cap_above_need' points above the need: a starving person is not content with food, however varied their pack.

work.name: Work
work._comment: Holding a job is worth very little by itself: the meter rises only while the person works their job (W), and sinks slowly toward 'idle_with_job' while they don't. How fast it rises: the right tools for the job (more than one, faster), how much choice of work the age offers, and how well they fit the job.

leaders.name: Leaders
leaders._comment: How they feel about the leaders: how well the offices are run, and everything else in their life (when food, safety, comfort and the rest go up, it reflects on the leaders, and faster while most of them are rising). Someone a leader appointed to work they are poorly suited for warms to the leaders only slowly; being dismissed or moved hurts a lot ('job_loss').

comfort.name: Comfort
comfort._comment: The tribe's Fire quality (raised only by people warming themselves at the fire, not by the fire merely burning), care from Healers and the Spirit Keeper, and shelter (once there are Builders). While the Spirit Keeper leads a ritual (their W work), everyone's comfort rises faster, and the tribe's care counts double (qualities 'while_working'). The input 'fire' (tended/untended/out, satisfaction.input_values) is still there for other meters.

safety.name: Safety
safety._comment: Warriors (and Scouts) watching over the camp, and every position in the tribe being filled. Each Warrior out on patrol right now makes it rise faster (and counts double toward the tribe's safety); while positions stand empty it rises slowly, or not at all.

expectations._comment: People get used to things. 'share' of each meter compares life with what they expect (50 = as expected); expectations follow reality at 'drift_per_day' per day-night cycle. 0 = no expectations.

job_loss._comment: What being dismissed from work costs. Anyone can be dismissed or moved to other work at any time, as often as the appointer likes, but people resent it. 'dismissed': taken off their work; 'reassigned': moved straight from one job to another by appointment. 'hit': points their meters drop at once. 'grievance': points their meters' targets stay lowered by, fading by half every 'grievance_half_life_life_hours' (of the day-night cycle); repeated dismissals add up, to at most 'max_grievance' per meter. 'onlookers': what everyone else feels each time (a leader who keeps dismissing people unsettles the whole tribe); a kind may set its own 'onlookers'. Unhappy people are restless: NPCs challenge or vote out leaders whose 'leaders' meter is low (npc.json 'discontent'), once their patience runs out ('patience').

reassigned._comment: Moving people between jobs is a normal part of leading (a food shortage, a new Toolmaker...): it costs a little Work contentment (leaving work they had got into), and onlookers don't mind it ('onlookers' here replaces the shared one). How they feel about the leaders depends on whether the new work is higher or lower ('job_rank').

job_rank._comment: How being appointed to work feels depends on where the new work stands in the hierarchy of work, not on being appointed at all. A job's rank: 'research_step' x how many research steps lie behind it (the longest chain of researched innovations it needs; ages' starting innovations don't count) + 'tools' if it needs tools; an office's: 'office_per_point' x its points. occupations.json or a government's office may set 'rank' outright. No work is rank 0. Moving up (say from no work, or Gatherer, to Hunter) raises the person's Leaders meter by 'up.hit' points per rank at once and leaves goodwill of 'up.goodwill' per rank (a grievance in reverse, fading the same way); moving down lowers it by 'down.hit' per rank and leaves a grievance of 'down.grievance' per rank. Same rank: no effect. At most 'max_points' per appointment. Dismissal is separate ('job_loss').

patience._comment: People put up with bad times for a while before they move against those in charge, so leaders get a chance to put things right. For each meter listed, a person's unrest is the cycle-hours their meter has spent below 'below'; it drains 'recover' times as fast while the meter is back above. Their discontent counts toward politics (challenges, persuasion, removal votes, outcasting, reform; npc.json 'discontent') only once unrest passes 'grace_life_hours', growing to full over the next 'build_up_life_hours'. 'warn_at': share of the grace used up when the chronicle warns that someone's patience is wearing thin.

leadership_training._comment: The office skill (character.json 'office_skill', leadership) for anyone holding an office. Each day they get practice x ('while_working' x how recently they worked their office with W, 1 fading to 0, see work.json 'work_counts_life_hours') + 'tribe_share' x the tribe's mood: (average 'meter' satisfaction - neutral_at) / span, between -1 and 1. So a leader who works the office gains, faster while the tribe is content; one who neglects it while the tribe is unhappy loses. Other office skills (an Elder's lore) grow only while working the office.
